text: The Gateway shall provide imagery and associated synchronized audio to the Crew.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Top-level requirement establishing the need for any Gateway-generated imagery (and associated audio, where applicable) to be made available to the crew.
label: Non-Causal

text: This requirement covers all imagery, internal, external, motion (video), and stills.
label: Non-Causal

text: Audio/Video Synchronization with the Gateway onboard clock can occur at the source or on the ground depending on implementation.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall record imagery with associated audio.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Top-level requirement establishing the need for any Gateway-generated imagery (and associated audio, where applicable) to be recorded onboard.
label: Causal

text: This requirement covers all imagery (internal & external), motion (video), and stills.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide imagery with associated audio to Exploration Systems.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Top-level requirement establishing the need for the Gateway vehicle to generate imagery (with associated audio, where applicable) and make that imagery available to other Exploration systems (Orion, Mission Systems, etc.).
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall comply with applicable requirements in DSG-SPEC-ECLS-007, Gateway Program Subsystem Specification for Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS).
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: An integrated Environmental Control and Life Support System will be implemented across Gateway to ensure habitability across all habitable volumes, including visiting vehicles attached and open to the Gateway.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway Program Subsystem Specification for ECLSS defines the specific functionality required of the ECLSS to enable top level capabilities, associated design standards, and module level functional and performance requirements.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall condition the atmosphere in habitable volumes and attached visiting vehicles to maintain temperature and humidity levels and to provide proper atmosphere circulation within the habitable volumes.
label: Causal

text: Rationale: Air conditioning includes circulation of air to ensure proper mixing, and maintaining the temperature and humidity levels within system capabilities.
label: Causal

text: This function must be performed during crewed and uncrewed periods to protect both crew and vehicle systems.
label: Causal

text: Further specification may be found in the Gateway ECLS Subsystem Specification.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide potable water for crew, system and payload use.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Potable water is necessary to maintain crew hydration during Gateway operations.
label: Causal

text: Water may also be needed for operating science and technology payloads, and other systems such as the EVA suit.
label: Causal

text: Water safety establishes that physiochemical and microbiological limits are met.
label: Non-Causal

text: Water quantity and delivery specifications will be defined in the DSG-SPEC-ECLS-007 ECLS Subsystem Specification and the Payload IRD.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide fire detection, suppression, isolation, and recovery for any internal fire events when there are potential flammable materials or ignition sources present, or credible oxygen enrichment.
label: Causal

text: Rationale: Fire protection includes fire prevention, fire detection and fire suppression.
label: Non-Causal

text: This capability is needed in both crewed and uncrewed mission phases.
label: Causal

text: End item fire protection is accomplished primarily by controlling flammable materials and ignition sources.
label: Causal

text: Flammable materials are controlled per NASA-STD-6016, Standard Materials and Processes Requirements for Spacecraft, and ignition sources are minimized via adherence to electrical design requirements such as proper bonding, grounding, wire and fuse sizing, and circuit protection.
label: Non-Causal

text: An ignition source is a source of heat sufficiently intense and localized to induce combustion.
label: Non-Causal

text: Any item that could cause sparks, such as a brush motor, is also considered an ignition source.
label: Non-Causal

text: If materials flammability and electrical requirements are not met, detection and suppression must be discussed during the safety review process.
label: Causal

text: Gateway shall maintain airborne contaminants below applicable limits for nominal human performance during crewed periods.
label: Causal

text: Rationale: Contaminants may be added to the atmosphere by crew, including carbon dioxide, particulates, and trace gases.
label: Non-Causal

text: Trace gases are added to the atmosphere through normal off-gassing from system surfaces.
label: Non-Causal

text: Additionally, particles associated with lunar regolith may be presented to the Gateway after a human lunar mission and through lunar sample return through the Science Airlock.
label: Causal

text: Specific capabilities and limits will be further defined in the Gateway ECLS Subsystem Specification.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall collect, contain, and dispose of crew bodily wastes.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: This requirement applies to the collection of crew metabolic waste associated with the toilet including urine, feces, vomit and other waste.
label: Non-Causal

text: While collection is only applicable during the crewed period, any long term storage may need to be managed during the uncrewed period.
label: Causal

text: It is expected that waste will be collected in the Habitation Element and may be transferred to another module, such as a LM, for long term storage and disposal.
label: Non-Causal

text: Venting of pretreated urine must be coordinated with structures and external systems, and must be balanced or non-propulsive to minimize Gateway stack attitude impulses.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide emergency equipment for crew survival, accessible within the time required to respond to the emergency.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: This is hardware needed in each element with hazards that might lead to a compromised atmosphere to allow crew to translate to a safe location within Gateway or the vehicle intended for crew return to Earth.
label: Causal

text: Efficient transit includes appropriate orientation with respect to doorways and hatches, as well as obstacle avoidance and illumination along the egress path.
label: Non-Causal

text: Hardware must be readily accessible to allow escape in the shortest amount of time.
label: Causal

text: Likewise an emergency lighting system must be automatically activated to allow operators and other occupants of a module to move to a safe location in the minimum amount of time.
label: Causal

text: The portable hardware classified as emergency equipment should be provided as Common Equipment to the modules to ensure commonality, compatibility, and portability.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall be designed to operate in atmospheric conditions with 0% humidity during uncrewed periods.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: During crewed operations, the dew point will remain within crew comfort levels.
label: Causal

text: During the uncrewed period, the cabin may be very dry with a dew point less than 4C (39F) at lowest allowable temperature.
label: Causal

text: Humidity may be removed purposefully to prevent condensation and microbial growth.
label: Causal

text: The humidity will passively be reduced as the pressure is maintained with dry gasses and no crew is present to replenish atmospheric vapor.
label: Causal

text: Appropriate design of electronics must be included to control electrostatic discharge (ESD) hazards.
label: Causal

text: Design Specifications to minimize risk of ESD may be found in DSG-RQMT-004, Gateway Electromagnetic Environmental Effects (E3) Requirements Document, and DSG- RQMT-007, Gateway Requirements for the Control of Electromagnetic Interference Characteristics of Subsystems and Equipment Document.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall operate in conditions up to 24.1% oxygen with nominal operating functions at the nominal atmospheric pressure of 101.3 kPa (14.7 psi).
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Enriched oxygen concentrations increase the flammability of materials within that environment.
label: Causal

text: Extensive flammability materials has been captured and is reflected in the NASA Materials Selection Database for flammability at this operating point.
label: Non-Causal

text: Oxygen concentration control ranges will be defined in the Gateway ECLS Subsystem Specification.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall operate in conditions up to 30% oxygen for atmosphere pressures up to 70 kPa (10.2 psia).
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Elevated oxygen concentrations are needed at lower pressures to sustain human life.
label: Causal

text: Oxygen concentration will be defined in the Gateway ECLS Subsystem Specification.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall maintain an internal habitable environment at pressures between 65 kPa (9.5 psia) to 102 kPa (14.9 psia); with the exception of airlocks.
label: Causal

text: Rationale: When crewed, the Gateway will be nominally maintained at pressures near to Earth sea level 101 kPa (14.7 psi).
label: Causal

text: The full range allows for operational flexibility during crewed and uncrewed periods, including response to contingency scenarios and potential reduction of consumables during uncrewed periods.
label: Causal

text: Pressurized modules have a design pressure for structural design purposes higher than 14.9 psia to account for pressure set points of positive pressure relief valves (PPRVs) and fault tolerance of the ECLS system.
label: Non-Causal

text: The required maximum design pressure for structural design is provided in the element and module allocated requirements sections.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall maintain interior atmosphere temperature to between 4°C (39°F) and 27°C (81°F).
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: This requirements establishes the full temperature control range for the Gateway during both crewed and uncrewed periods.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway will maintain temperatures according to crew capability during crewed mission phases.
label: Causal

text: These ranges will be further specified in the Gateway ECLS Subsystem Specification.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall equalize the pressure between adjacent isolated modules.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Vestibule pressurization is required prior to hatch opening between modules and to allow a visiting vehicle to be opened to the Gateway Habitation Element.
label: Causal

text: This is required during crewed and uncrewed mission phases.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall limit disturbances caused by venting of fluids and gasses per the <TBD-L2- GW-059> table.
label: Causal

text: Rationale: Nominal ECLS functions include venting of waste gases and fluids from ECLS systems and payloads.
label: Non-Causal

text: Additional venting would occur with nominal venting associated with pressure control functions, included reduction in in the internal atmosphere pressure, depressurization of vestibules to support departure of visiting vehicles, and airlock operations.
label: Non-Causal

text: Thermal Control Subsystem capable of maintaining its own equipment within thermal limits at all times for any flight attitude.
label: Non-Causal

text: Modules within the Habitation Element will be capable of sharing thermal control resources with an adjacent module for flexibility during contingencies.
label: Causal

text: Each module may utilize active and/or passive thermal control methods to meet thermal requirements.
label: Causal

text: Thermal Control Subsystem Specification defines the specific functionality required to enable top level capabilities, associated design standards, and element/module level functional and performance requirements.
label: Non-Causal

text: Thermal Control System that maintains all habitable volumes and internal and external components within thermal limits.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Each Element/Module in the integrated Gateway stack must maintain its components, both internal and external, within thermal limits.
label: Non-Causal

text: Any modules with habitable volumes must also maintain the internal environment within thermal limits for both crewed and uncrewed operations.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall operate within thermal limits independent of flight attitude.
label: Non-Causal

text: The integrated Gateway stack must have the flexibility to be pointed in any direction to support mission objectives.
label: Non-Causal

text: Thermal Control System to operate within thermal limits at any attitude necessary, making its performance flight attitude independent.
label: Causal

text: However, indefinite duration capability at any attitude is not possible, so duration limits must be established and provided to stakeholders.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall apply an architecture that provides for module thermal independence during non-contingency operations.
label: Causal

text: Rationale: Each Module's TCS will need to be responsible for its own thermal independence and ability to manage its own heatloads during nominal operations.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall have crew hatches in accordance with DSG-SPEC-HTCH-019, Gateway Program Subsystem Specification for Hatches.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Providing a common set of functional requirements for all Gateway crew hatches simplifies crew training, eases operations, increases reliability of operation, and streamlines the development process by providing a ready set of base requirements for an end item specification.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall continuously record structural dynamic responses at discrete locations and process data to assess structural life consumption and perform damage detection, location, and assessment.
label: Causal

text: The structural health monitoring system is required to measure responses of the Gateway to actual dynamic loads in order to assess structural life usage vs predicted loads.
label: Causal

text: Knowledge of life state can be used to modify operations to either add constraints to protect structural life or to reduce un-needed constraints.
label: Causal

text: Due to limitations on crew time and other Gateway resources, automated structural damage detection, location, and assessment can be utilized to determine criticality of damage and focus remediation efforts.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall limit atmospheric leakage rate to less than 0.05 kg/day at ambient pressure in isolated module configuration.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: This leakage rate is consistent with ISS experience and reflects the leakage of multiple elements aggregated on-orbit.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall detect atmospheric leaks greater than <TBD-L2-GW-011>.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Detection of leaks will allow for response and repair, in the event of an atmospheric leak, by the crew or autonomously.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall localize atmospheric leaks to within <TBD-L2-GW-012> location in any pressurized habitable volume.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Localization of leaks will allow for response and repair, in the event of an atmospheric leak, by the crew during crewed periods or autonomously during uncrewed periods.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall have an 800mm -0.3mm/+unlimited diameter transfer passageway between modules mated with the Gateway Docking System (GDS), as described in the DSG-SPEC- MECH-017, Gateway Program Docking System Specification.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: DSG-SPEC-MECH-017, Gateway Program Docking System Specification compliant mechanisms only provide an 800mm diameter passageway for a distance of 3-4 ft when mated.
label: Causal

text: Items to be transferred between Gateway Elements need to be sized appropriately.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall be equipped with passive or active crew exercise equipment isolation systems to reduce induced loads to the primary structure to less than or equal to <TBD-L2-GW- Gateway structure.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall have a Probability of No Penetration (PNP) greater than or equal to for items with the potential to create a catastrophic hazard if impacted or punctured by MMOD.
label: Causal

text: Rationale: This requirement sets the limit for the probability of no penetration.
label: Non-Causal

text: This requirement is based upon the ISS PNP requirement for permanent modules.
label: Non-Causal

text: Area is the outer most surface area of the module and is in m^2 and Time is in years.
label: Non-Causal

text: Time used for calculation should encompass the expected life of the module.
label: Non-Causal

text: For the purposes of MMOD, a penetration is defined as damage/failure to stored energy devices that causes a hazard to crew or Gateway survivability.
label: Causal

text: Typically, penetration is defined as a partial or complete perforation of the pressure vessel or casing, detached spall from the pressure vessel wall, damage to the pressure vessel that would allow unstable crack growth, or deformation of a casing of rotating machinery such that the deformation could intrude into the dynamic envelope of the rotating device.
label: Causal

text: For metallic tank pressure vessels, critical damage is defined as a penetration depth in the pressure shell of 20% of the thickness of the pressure shell.
label: Non-Causal

text: For composite overwrapped pressure vessels, critical damage is defined as penetration of 90% of the composite overwrap thickness.
label: Non-Causal

text: Solar array panels are not included in this requirement.
label: Non-Causal

text: The meteoroid environment is defined in NASA/TM-2015-218214, NASA Meteoroid Engineering Model Release 2.0, and the orbital debris environment is defined in NASA/TP-2015-218592, NASA Orbital Debris Engineering Model.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide at least single failure tolerance to catastrophic events.
label: Non-Causal

text: Catastrophic hazards that cannot be controlled using failure tolerance may be exempted from the failure tolerance requirements with mandatory concurrence from the Technical Authorities and Director, Johnson Space Center (JSC) (for crew risk acceptance).
label: Causal

text: Exemptions from failure tolerance shall be requested in accordance with DSG-RQMT-011, Gateway Hazard Analysis Requirements.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Compliance with this requirement can be accomplished at the end item level or through a combination of hazard controls at the Module/System levels and end item level.
label: Causal

text: A common way to improve reliability and thus meet safety requirements is to use systems that tolerate failures when complete failure avoidance isn’t practical.
label: Causal

text: Specific hazard controls and implementation must be derived from an integrated design and safety analysis performed in accordance with DSG-RQMT-011, Gateway Hazard Analysis Requirements.
label: Non-Causal

text: Acceptance of these approaches by the Technical Authorities avoids processing waivers for numerous hazard causes where failure tolerance is not the appropriate approach.
label: Causal

text: Additional failure tolerance may be required to meet systems reliability requirements.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide the capability for autonomous operation of system and subsystem functions, which if lost, would result in a catastrophic event.
label: Causal

text: Rationale: This capability means that the system does not depend on communication with Earth (e.g., mission control) to perform functions that are required for control of catastrophic hazards.
label: Non-Causal

text: While the crew is present, the Gateway should automate catastrophic hazard controls to minimize the need for crew actions, using crew action only as a last resort where automation is not practical.
label: Causal

text: Rationale: Critical hazards do not require failure tolerance for human-rating, however, critical hazards can have a significant impact on Loss of Mission (LOM) risk.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway Program will derive the specific hazard controls and implementation from an integrated design and safety analysis performed in accordance with DSG-RQMT-011.
label: Non-Causal

text: Failure tolerance for critical hazards may be required to meet probability of loss of mission or system reliability requirements (if applicable).
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide the appropriate failure tolerance capability without the use of emergency equipment and systems.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Emergency systems, EVA or emergency operations cannot be used as a leg of failure tolerance as these emergency systems and equipment cannot definitively prevent an initiating event.
label: Causal

text: As a result, the mitigation of catastrophic and critical hazards will implement a FT strategy without the use of EVA, emergency systems, or emergency operations.
label: Causal

text: However, the use of EVA, emergency systems, and contingency or emergency operations will be considered a Crew Survival Method (CSM) to prevent Loss of Crew (LOC) in the event all other approved hazard controls have failed.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall protect redundant systems, redundant subsystems, and redundant major elements of subsystems (such as assemblies, panels, power supplies, tanks, controls, and associated interconnecting wiring and fluid lines) to ensure that an unexpected event which damages one is not likely to prevent the other from performing the functions.
label: Causal

text: Rationale: Where redundancy is used to satisfy the failure tolerance requirement, this design requirement provides maximum protection from common cause events.
label: Causal

text: This requirement does not mandate physical separation but physical separation has been a historically demonstrated method to mitigate common cause failures.
label: Non-Causal

text: System analysis needs to consider the channelization of all capabilities necessary to manage Fault, Detection, Isolation and Recovery (FDIR) including sensors and utility services such as power, thermal and data.
label: Causal

text: Rationale: For NASA sponsored end items the risk of human casualty on the ground is limited to less than 1 in 10,000 as required per NASA-STD-8719.14A, Process for Limiting Orbital Debris.
label: Non-Causal

text: The NASA-STD is a companion to NPR 8715.6 and provides specific requirements and assessment methods to assure compliance with the NPR.
label: Causal

text: The principal factors used in calculating the risk of human casualty from uncontrolled reentries include the number of debris expected to reach the surface of the Earth, the kinetic energy of each surviving debris, and the amount of the world population potentially at risk.
label: Non-Causal

text: The last factor is a function of both the orbital inclination of the space structure prior to re-entry and the year in which the re-entry occurs.
label: Non-Causal

text: Extensive human casualty studies by the U.S. Government, including the Department of Defense and the Department of Energy, have examined the probability of injury and/or death from falling debris for a variety of impacting kinetic energies to humans.
label: Non-Causal

text: A kinetic energy threshold criterion of 15 joules is widely accepted as the minimum level for potential injury to an unprotected person.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall comply with the requirements in DSG-SPEC-CHP-010, Gateway Program Subsystem Specification for Crew Health and Performance (CHP).
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: DSG-SPEC-CHP-010 includes content decomposed from requirements in DSG-RQMT-001 regarding crew health and performance.
label: Non-Causal

text: This specification addresses aspects of crew health and performance such as Medical Capability, Environmental Health, Behavioral Health, Wellness Support, Crew Performance Capability, Countermeasures, and CHP Data Integration across all Gateway modules and includes an applicability Matrix denoting applicability to specific Gateway Elements.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide a habitable volume that accommodates crew living and working tasks.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: To maintain a habitable volume and high level of mission performance and safety, it is important that the architectural layout of the vehicle is functionally designed to provide defined locations and volumes that allow for expected crew activities, including mission operations, habitability functions, and translation (for example, movement between areas).
label: Causal

text: Required volume is a function of the number of crewmembers, number of mission and contingency days, and crew operations (both nominal and off-nominal).
label: Non-Causal

text: Adequate internal size, in terms of volume and surface area, needs to be provided to ensure expected number of crewmembers can safely, efficiently, and effectively perform mission tasks, including, but not limited to, work, sleep, eat, personal hygiene, private crew areas, translation, egress, ingress, pressurized suit donning, emergency medical treatment, and other tasks necessary for a safe and successful mission.
label: Causal

text: Mission and volume designers are to carefully analyze volume needs of the crew, crew equipment, storage, trash containment volumes and trash transition plans to ensure they are adequately sized to provide adequate net habitable volume for the crew to effectively and efficiently perform mission objectives.
label: Causal

text: Every effort should be made to separate functional areas for activities that could degrade or operationally conflict with each other, particularly emergency response activities, or that produce environmental conditions that are detrimental to mission performance or safety (for example, glare, noise, vibrations, heat, odors, etc.).
label: Causal

text: Co-location of unrelated activities could degrade operations resulting in increased workload and operational delays.
label: Causal

text: Furthermore, traffic flow is not to interfere with other unrelated operational and recreational activities of the crew.
label: Non-Causal

text: These activities may include sensitive spacecraft control, routine servicing, experimentation, eating, sleep, and relaxation.
label: Non-Causal

text: Similarly, co-location of related, sequential functional work areas can reduce transit time, communication errors, and operational delays.
label: Causal

text: For example, food stowage and food preparation areas should be located near one another to minimize the time required to retrieve food for meals and promote group dining for behavioral health benefits; and consistent spatial orientation and visual distinctions such as identifiers and aids can promote effective execution of mission tasking.
label: Causal

text: The management of crew nutrition is defined as influencing the design, provision, and operational implementation of in-flight nourishment of crewmembers over the course of the mission to perform Gateway tasks.
label: Non-Causal

text: Nutrition capabilities include provisions for food and food hydration, crew hydration, storage and preparation facilities, dining accommodations (group meals), tracking of nutritional intake, food system training, and implementation of individualized or standard in-flight menus.
label: Non-Causal

text: Nutrition also includes management of food system quality (food acceptability and metabolic intake (Intravehicular Activity (IVA) and EVA)), food safety (food micro-organism levels, cross-contamination prevention, cross-contamination separation), and food preparation (heating, rehydration, dining accommodations, in-flight food preparation time), and clean-up (food system waste, food system spill control, food system cleaning and sanitizing).
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall manage crew medical care, per DSG-SPEC-CHP-010, Gateway Program Subsystem Specification for CHP.
label: Non-Causal

text: The management of medical care is defined as influencing the design, provision, and operational implementation of the relevant in-flight medical capabilities.
label: Non-Causal

text: Medical care capabilities include clinical care, imaging, laboratory management, and pharmacy management, wellness support, and an integrated crew health and performance data system.
label: Non-Causal

text: Clinical care provides in-flight capabilities for the prevention, diagnosis, treatment, monitoring, and long-term management of medical conditions.
label: Non-Causal

text: Imaging provides in-flight capabilities for diagnostic imaging in support of the provision of clinical care and includes all hardware, software, and analysis capabilities required for the capturing and processing of diagnostic imaging.
label: Non-Causal

text: Laboratory management provides in-flight capabilities for laboratory analysis in support of the provision of clinical care and includes all hardware, software, and analysis capabilities required for the collection and processing of biological samples.
label: Non-Causal

text: Pharmacy management provides in-flight capabilities for the administration of pharmaceuticals in support of clinical care and includes all medications and the mechanisms used to prepare and deliver them and track their use.
label: Non-Causal

text: Wellness support capabilities include functions required to promote, maintain, and protect the physical and mental well-being of the crewmembers.
label: Non-Causal

text: This support comes in the form of physiological health management, nutrition management, behavioral support, and sleep management.
label: Non-Causal

text: Medical care also encompasses two-way private voice and video communication with Mission Systems.
label: Non-Causal

text: Also under medical care are the capabilities and plans for handling deceased crewmembers that are socially, biologically, and physically acceptable.
label: Non-Causal

text: NASA-STD-3001, Volume 1, includes definitions of the levels of medical care required to reduce the risk that exploration missions are impacted by crew medical issues and to ensure that long-term astronaut health risks are managed within acceptable limits.
label: Non-Causal

text: As mission duration and complexity increase, the capability required to prevent and manage medical contingencies correspondingly increases.
label: Causal

text: The ability to provide the designated level of care applies to all flight phases, including during pressurized suited operations.
label: Non-Causal

text: A medical system provides preventive care, diagnostic care, and medical treatment and must consider any possible in-flight medical need including persistent health conditions.
label: Non-Causal

text: Additional information on Levels of Care can be found in NASA/TM- System Development.
label: Non-Causal

text: To date, there have been multiple illnesses and injuries during all mission phases and, in the absence of adequate clinical capabilities, the likelihood of significant negative impact to mission viability due to crewmember illness or injury is increased.
label: Causal

text: Because immediate transport to a clinical facility is not an option on-orbit, in flight health care is essential and is optimal with an integrated crew health data system, to support the detection, diagnosis, and treatment of illness and injury.
label: Causal

text: An integrated crew health data system aids in the management of crew health in-flight, especially for the early detection and intervention for medical issues.
label: Non-Causal

text: During missions with longer evacuation times and mission duration, the management of data, information, and ability for extensible knowledge augmentation becomes increasingly important in order to manage the medical care and wellness of the crew efficiently.
label: Causal

text: To aid the crew in basic decision support through automatic organization of data and knowledge augmentation materials (such as medical references), an integrated system should collect, process, and store all crew health-relevant data from various sources (vehicle and ground), in addition to crew task performance data, and make this data available to both the crewmembers and ground support.
label: Causal

text: Necessary capabilities include data sources interfaces for secure data collection, data storage, descriptive analytics, advanced analytics, and data user interfaces.
label: Non-Causal

text: Descriptive analytics provides in-flight capabilities for modelling and analytics, data mining, discovery and search and report generation.
label: Non-Causal

text: Advanced analytics can provide in-flight capabilities to store knowledge bases and provide basic decision support functionality.
label: Non-Causal

text: Data user interfaces provides in-flight capabilities for the crewmembers to interface with the vehicle's habitat data infrastructure, including messaging, data input, and display.
label: Non-Causal

text: The management of crew behavioral health is defined as influencing the design, provision, and operational implementation of in-flight behavioral health.
label: Non-Causal

text: Behavioral health capabilities include the assessment, monitoring, and intervention pertaining to psychological adaptation, workload, sleep and fatigue issues, key relationships (e.g., relationships with family and friends, intra-crew relationships, and relationships between the crew and ground), and behavioral medicine.
label: Non-Causal

text: Also includes the implementation of individually-tailored countermeasures, support of work/life balance, provision of leisure activities, delivery of family support services, provision of private crew areas, motivation, alertness, cognition, and adaptation of the crewmember during flight.
label: Non-Causal

text: Behavioral health management is needed to prevent and ameliorate the deleterious effects of living in an isolated and confined space and to preserve both individual and “crew as a unit” behavioral health and performance and cohesive functionality.
label: Causal

text: The management of crew behavioral health includes: design, provision, operational implementation, and hardware/software that is necessary to provide in-flight behavioral health support.
label: Non-Causal

text: Behavioral health and performance capabilities include assessment, monitoring, and mitigation strategies are related to psychological adaptation and dependent on workload, sleep and fatigue issues.
label: Non-Causal

text: Providing individualized countermeasures to support work/life balance, private crew areas, leisure activities and family support services are dependent on the crew member’s alertness, cognition, motivation, and adaptation.
label: Non-Causal

text: The management of crew sleep is defined as the design, provision, and operational implementation of in-flight sleep capabilities.
label: Non-Causal

text: Sleep capabilities include, but not limited to, sleep accommodations that are temperature controlled and that eliminate noise and light pollution, schedules for sleep shifting for mission essential tasks, variable wavelength light assemblies, software supporting electronic devices with visual displays consistent with circadian rhythm lighting requirements, prevention of fatigue-induced performance errors, and preservation of the ability of crewmembers to respond in contingency situations.
label: Non-Causal

text: Sleep maintenance includes blue blocking glasses, and properly ground tested medications including but not limited to: chronobiologic, alertness, sedative- hypnotics, soporifics and control of ambient environmental factors.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall manage crew physiological health.
label: Non-Causal

text: The management of crew physiological health is defined as influencing the design, provision, and operational implementation of in-flight pre, in, and post-flight countermeasures systems to mitigate risks to crew health and performance.
label: Non-Causal

text: Physiological health capabilities include activities such as exercise, hygiene, and other conditioning and countermeasures against physiological disturbances to body systems (e.g., musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal, genitourinary, neurovestibular, ocular, hearing, immune, and reproductive).
label: Non-Causal

text: Pre-flight, in-flight, and post-flight countermeasures shall include resistance and aerobic exercise hardware, sensorimotor preservation hardware and software systems, exercise software, nutritional supplementation, pharmaceutical supplementation, and human health and performance software optimization tools.
label: Non-Causal

text: Nutritional / pharmaceutical supplementation may include provision of additional caloric content, specific macronutrients, and/or other pharmaceutical supplementation to the existing food system.
label: Non-Causal

text: These may be used pre, in, and post flight and factors including shelf life, and storage should be incorporated in nutritional tracking software.
label: Non-Causal

text: Human health and performance optimization tools will require incorporation of vehicle systems data and other CHP systems data in a data management system that will allow for running existing algorithms to inform/predict crew health and performance capabilities.
label: Causal

text: Incorporating this information into display/informatics systems is critical.
label: Non-Causal

text: The intent of this specific countermeasures is to align with the phased approach of using Gateway as a proving ground to develop tools for improved crew autonomy.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway system shall limit cross-contamination between food preparation areas and body waste management and hygiene areas.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Limiting the transfer of microorganisms to the food preparation areas protects crew health.
label: Causal

text: To properly control the contamination of the food preparation area from the body waste management and hygiene areas, a task analysis must be performed to identify important design factors (i.e. concurrent use of the areas, volume needed at each location to prevent contact, distance between areas, storage and accessibility requirements, etc.).
label: Causal

text: The chance of cross-contamination can be further decreased by designating body waste management and personal hygiene areas as far away from food preparation areas as possible.
label: Non-Causal

text: While vehicle design constraints may limit the distance between the areas, measures must be in place to prevent food contamination during preparation, such as a higher quality body waste containment and isolation system.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall protect crew from toxicological hazards.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Environmental hazard protection includes capabilities to measure, monitor, assess, alert, and respond to toxicological concerns in the Gateway atmosphere.
label: Non-Causal

text: Toxicological protection ensures in-flight capabilities for toxicological monitoring, assessment, and mitigation in Gateway air and water.
label: Causal

text: Additional examples include provisions of personal protective equipment for crew survival in a compromised atmosphere, data recording and display, fire detection, warning, and extinguishing, and emergency equipment accessibility.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall protect crew from microbial hazards.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Environmental hazard protection includes capabilities to measure, monitor, assess, alert, and respond to microbial concerns in the Gateway atmosphere.
label: Non-Causal

text: Microbial environmental protection ensures in-flight capabilities for monitoring and mitigating microbial contamination in the air, water, and surfaces as well as capabilities for decontamination.
label: Causal

text: This also includes the capability to maintain personal hygiene and have adequate food and waste storage.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall protect crew from acoustic hazards.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Environmental hazard protection includes capabilities to measure, monitor, assess, alert, and respond to acoustic concerns in the Gateway atmosphere.
label: Non-Causal

text: Acoustic environmental protection ensures in-flight capabilities for monitoring, assessing, and mitigating harmful acoustic environments through hearing protection and acoustic and vibrational dampening countermeasures.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall protect crew from radiation hazards.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Environmental hazard protection includes capabilities to measure, monitor, assess, alert, and respond to radiation concerns in the Gateway atmosphere.
label: Non-Causal

text: Radiation environmental protection ensures in-flight capabilities for the monitoring and provision of alerts and warnings for the space weather (ionizing radiation) environment.
label: Causal

text: This also includes protection from, and treatment of, exposure to highly ionizing radiation environments, in addition to capabilities to maintain safe levels of non-ionizing radiation exposure.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall maintain a shirt sleeve environment in all habitable volumes during crewed missions.
label: Causal

text: Rationale: A safe, breathable atmosphere is critical to crew health and performance.
label: Non-Causal

text: Monitoring atmospheric quality, alerting ground and crew of off-nominal conditions, and evaluating environmental data trends during vehicle flight operations is essential to crew health support.
label: Non-Causal

text: The vehicle system needs to be robust enough to control or allow crew control of atmospheric pressure, humidity, temperature, ventilation flow rate, airborne particulates, partial pressure of O2, CO2, and trace contaminants within ranges necessary to maintain human health and safety.
label: Non-Causal

text: The vehicle must also be robust enough to maintain safe, comfortable atmospheric conditions within physiological ranges during crew induced thermal loading such as exercise.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall manage expected biological hazards.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Management is defined as influencing the design, provision, and operational implementation of the capability for controlling biological hazards.
label: Non-Causal

text: Biological hazards include blood, bodily fluids, medical equipment, and sharp items.
label: Non-Causal

text: If not properly contained, contents could damage equipment, injure crewmembers, and transmit disease.
label: Causal

text: Biological waste, including vomit and feminine hygiene products, can also cause injury and transmit disease.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall incorporate window(s) in a habitable element for crew viewing that maximize views of both the Moon and Earth measuring no less than 50.8 centimeters (20 inches) in diameter.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: This requirement supports crew psychological health, vehicle inspection, and public outreach.
label: Non-Causal

text: The window size supports simultaneous use by two crewmembers and is consistent with the window currently in the ISS U.S.
label: Non-Causal

text: More than one window may be required as the nominal Gateway NRHO orbit and SPEA attitude constrains observations (duration, distance, and look angle) for any single window.
label: Non-Causal

text: While attitude changes can optimize window views, no propellant has been allocated for maneuvers and CMG desaturations.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall tolerate an inadvertent operator action, as identified by a human error analysis (HEA), without causing a catastrophic event.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: An operator is defined as any human that commands or interfaces with the space system during the mission, including humans in the control centers.
label: Non-Causal

text: The appropriate level of protection (i.e., one, two, or more inadvertent actions) is determined by an integrated human error and hazard analysis.
label: Non-Causal

text: This requirement is not intended to prevent operators from initially selecting the wrong control.
label: Non-Causal

text: The system needs to ensure the crew can recover from inadvertent input with minimal impact by incorporating the capability for undoing control input.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall tolerate inadvertent operator action in the presence of any single system failure.
label: Causal

text: The intent of this requirement is to provide a robust human-system interface design that cannot be defeated by a system failure.
label: Non-Causal

text: Where the system is designed to protect for more than one inadvertent action, the level of protection after a single system failure may be reduced - but still protects from a single inadvertent operator action.
label: Causal

text: In addition, this ensures that back-up capabilities, such as back-up flight software, maintain the same-level of tolerance to human error as the primary system.
label: Causal

text: Prevent human error in the maintenance, operation, and control of the system.
label: Non-Causal

text: Design the system to limit the negative effects of errors.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Human error is either an action that is not intended or desired by the human or a failure on the part of the human to perform a prescribed action within specified limits of accuracy, sequence or time that fails to produce the expected result and has led or has the potential to lead to an unwanted consequence.
label: Non-Causal

text: Controlling Human Error requires identification of human errors through human error analysis (HEA).
label: Non-Causal

text: The HEA is a systematic approach to evaluate human actions, identify potential human error, model human performance, and qualitatively characterize how human error affects a system.
label: Non-Causal

text: HEA provides an evaluation of human actions and error in an effort to generate system improvements that reduce the frequency of error and minimize the negative effects on the system.
label: Causal

text: The human error analysis considers mission operations while the crew is interacting with the space system - including crew operations, ground control operations (typically covered via hazard reports), and ground processing operations with flight crew interfaces.
label: Non-Causal

text: The analysis also covers response to system failures and abort scenarios.
label: Non-Causal

text: Identify other types of human error that would result in a catastrophic event (e.g., operational errors, errors of omission, timing errors).
label: Non-Causal

text: Apply the appropriate error management as described in this requirement.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall protect crew from decompression sickness (DCS).
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway systems and ConOps must protect crew from DCS related to pressure changes for EVA operations (including preparation and return) and off-nominal depressurization situations.
label: Non-Causal

text: DCS risk limits are defined in NASA-STD-3001 Volume 1 paragraph 4.4.3.6.1 DCS Prevention.
label: Non-Causal

text: This requirement works together with V2 6009 DCS Treatment Capability and V2 11032 LEA Suited DCS Prevention Capability.
label: Non-Causal

text: For EVA operations, the DCS prevention design must be coordinated for total pressure, ppO2, and pre-breath protocol between all vehicles/elements inhabited by EVA crew prior to and after EVA (e.g., Orion, Gateway, Airlock, Lander).
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall comply with applicable requirements in DSG-SPEC-CS-006, Gateway Program Subsystem Specification for Crew Systems.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Crew Systems system includes IVA subsystems such as galley, housekeeping, crew hygiene, restraints and mobility aids, crew sleep, stowage, inventory management, tools and maintenance, and trash management.
label: Non-Causal

text: Some of these subsystems are distributed across multiple Gateway modules and are desired to function with crew and IVR.
label: Non-Causal

text: The specification levies some Crew Systems requirements to multiple modules, identifying each requirement’s module allocation.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide for crew to conduct personal hygiene.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Personal hygiene includes body and hair washing, shaving, dental hygiene, and changing clothes in a private volume.
label: Non-Causal

text: The volume should be separate from sleep and body waste management volumes.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide a trash management system to contain expected trash and evolved gases.
label: Non-Causal

text: The trash management system must contain all trash, including hazardous waste, with appropriate wrappings and/or barriers that is usable by crew and does not allow inadvertent release of trash into the habitable volume.
label: Causal

text: If not properly contained, trash contents could damage equipment, injure crewmembers, or transmit disease.
label: Causal

text: Operations analysis should be performed to drive trash containment design.
label: Causal

text: Analysis should evaluate all crew tasks that will generate trash over the duration of a mission, including ascent and return.
label: Causal

text: The trash containment design should consider crew usability, how and where trash will be stowed, duration of stowage until disposal, and method of disposal.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide an inventory management system (IMS).
label: Non-Causal

text: Inventory management allows the identification of flight equipment in specified locations to maintain organization and efficiency for the crew or IVR, and to identify usage and usage rates for usage and resupply decisions for the crew and ground support.
label: Causal

text: IMS needs to assist in tracking and potentially locating logistics, cargo, payload, or utilization items, and provides logistics awareness to ground support.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide a stowage system that can be monitored via the IMS.
label: Non-Causal

text: The stowage system does not include vehicle secondary structure.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall accommodate restraints and mobility aids for IVA operations.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Without gravity to hold an individual on a standing or sitting surface, the body naturally moves in the opposite direction of an applied force.
label: Causal

text: The cognitive and physical work required to maintain body position during a task can interfere with the task performance.
label: Causal

text: Mobility aids, such as hand and foot restraints, allow crew-members to efficiently move from one location to another in 0 g, as well as reduce the likelihood of inadvertent collision into hardware that may cause damage to the vehicle or injury to the crew.
label: Causal

text: Mobility aids must be designed to accommodate a pressurized suited crew-member, a non-suited crew-member, and IVR assets by providing clearance, non-slip surfaces, and non-circular cross sections.
label: Non-Causal

text: Without predefined mobility aids, personnel will use available equipment that may be damaged from induced loads.
label: Causal

text: The restraints and mobility aids should be compatible with IVR.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide for self-rescue of an EVA crewperson who becomes separated from the Gateway spacecraft.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Safety Tether is the primary means of crew restraint for EVA.
label: Non-Causal

text: An EVA crewmember could become separated from the Gateway (i.e. if the crewmember loses grip or comes out of the foot restraint AND if the safety tether breaks or is improperly configured).
label: Non-Causal

text: If the combination of these happen, the crewmember would need a self-rescue method for survival to return to the Gateway.
label: Causal

text: Orion does not support astronaut egress or ingress for EVA (nominal or contingency) from the crew module.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway EVA capability is needed to support external contingency maintenance operations, EVA system demonstrations, and payload and utilization needs.
label: Causal

text: EVAs may be nominal (pre-planned prior to the crewed mission) or contingency (responding to an off-nominal scenario which arises during the mission).
label: Non-Causal

text: EVA support includes the capability to deliver and prepare the EVA suits, ingress and egress the gateway while minimizing the loss of cabin atmosphere, translation and post-EVA suit maintenance and stowage.
label: Non-Causal

text: EVA operations will be available once the Gateway airlock module is added to the Gateway and EVA suits are present.
label: Causal

text: Nominal maintenance operations and utilization operations will be performed by EVR.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall establish EVA worksites <TBR-L2-GW-013>.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Worksites will be assessed as the design matures to determine if they require handrails, Body Restraint Tether (BRT), Worksite Interface (WIF), Articulating Portable Foot Restraint (APFR) i.e. dedicated vs. free-float.
label: Causal

text: Worksites <TBR-L2-GW-013> could include EVR backup and utilization.
label: Non-Causal

text: Further analysis will be done on forces, torques, envelopes, and LPGF clocking, etc., to support manipulator end-effector requirements and design.
label: Causal

text: The specific number and placement of LPGF's will be determined through joint, integrated analysis by the Contractor and NASA.
label: Non-Causal

text: The total number of SORI-OVs to be placed on the PPE is dependent on the PPE design and integrated Gateway utilization philosophy and will be determined through an integrated assessment with Gateway.
label: Causal

text: An integrated analysis will be performed to determine worksite locations based on Gateway system and module needs.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall comply with interface requirements in DSG-IRD-EVA-008, Gateway Program Extravehicular Activity (EVA) Compatibility Interface Requirements.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: HEOMD-004, Human Exploration Requirements, specifies the Gateway shall provide the capability for EVA operations.
label: Non-Causal

text: EVA interfaces are designed to be compatible with EVA operations.
label: Non-Causal

text: This includes restraining the crewmember, safeguarding both the vehicle and crewmember while working, and accommodating EVA contingency operations using a standard EVA tool set.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall accommodate EVA capability without blocking access to the visiting crewed vehicle(s) during the EVA.
label: Causal

text: Rationale: During prebreathe operations, campout, or if the need arises to depress equipment lock as secondary ingress path, an airlock situated in between the stack and the crewed vehicle isolates IVA crew from the VV or indicates they have to sit in the VV (and may not be able to command Airlock repress from that side).
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide EVA compatible accommodations to support continuous translation across adjacent (berthed/docked) modules.
label: Causal

text: Rationale: EVA translation across the Gateway stack is necessary to support both EVA test objectives and contingency EVAs regardless of the status of EVR capabilities.
label: Causal

text: Translation aids, such as EVA Handrails, and a path free of obstructions or hazards must be designed to support the movement of EVA crew members between the crew lock and EVA work sites.
label: Non-Causal

text: Each module is responsible for linking translation paths between modules.
label: Non-Causal

text: This may result in the need for handrails to be installed around the circumference of the end of each module and/or extending radial towards the end-cone or docking adapter.
label: Causal

text: It is not assumed that each module will have a consistent “clocking” of translation paths, therefore a flexible design solution may be necessary depending on the stack architecture.
label: Causal

text: Reference DSG-IRD-EVA-008 for EVA translation path requirements to ensure that the translation paths are designed in accordance to be compatible with the suit.
label: Non-Causal

text: An integrated analysis will be performed to optimize continuous translation paths across the integrated Gateway system.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide recharge services for at least two-crew EVA suits two times per crewed mission.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Part of enabling EVA is servicing the EVA suits.
label: Non-Causal

text: Servicing and checkout of the suits are performed between EVAs on a maintenance schedule and proceeding any EVA, including recharging consumables.
label: Non-Causal

text: Vehicle services to the suit are included through an umbilical interface panel and umbilicals in the Airlock.
label: Non-Causal

text: Supporting prebreathe and volume for suit don/doff, and suit stowage are necessary to support EVAs.
label: Causal

text: The EVR IRDD provides the interoperability requirements to enable common robotic interface installation on modules, ORUs and payloads.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide power, data, video, structural support and thermal services, as applicable, to external robotically compatible equipment, during all phases of operation.
label: Causal

text: The external robotics includes a set of worksite/payload interface equipment (including SORI) that transfers these services from Gateway modules to payloads.
label: Non-Causal

text: These services will also be provided during manipulation (except thermal control).
label: Causal

text: Thermal services are specifically transfer of ATCS fluid.
label: Non-Causal

text: An integrated analysis will be performed to determine the location of translation paths.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide worksites for external robotics operations in accordance with CSA- GWY-ID-0001.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: EVR operations to remove and install equipment require work areas that are designed for robotic compatibility.
label: Non-Causal

text: Worksites implies both the contact regions where equipment is installed and the surrounding area which must have clearance and inadvertent contact resistance.
label: Non-Causal

text: Operations include but are not limited to inspection.
label: Non-Causal

text: A Gateway integrated analysis will be performed to identify where EVR worksites will be located to support Gateway operations.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall have external ORUs that are compatible with robotics per the EVR Interface Requirements and Definition Document CSA-GWY-ID-0001.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Gateway EVA is available on a contingency basis only, therefore any external ORUs must plan for robotics to be the primary means for installation and removal.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall autonomously perform off-loading and re-loading of external logistics vehicles.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway will provide a capability to off-load the external ORUs and experimental payloads that can be used without requiring crew or constant ground communication.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide external robotically compatible attachment locations that provide services for ORUs, systems, and payloads during all ORU/payload life-cycle phases: operation, non-operation, external stowage, robotic manipulation and any others.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: External robotically-compatible attachment locations with standard SORI, LPGF, and LORI fixtures will be used for ORUs for Gateway maintenance, external cargo not used immediately on delivery by the Logistics Module (or other source), and active payload instruments and hardware.
label: Non-Causal

text: Multiple instruments may be hosted on a single SORI or LPGF, assuming the instruments stay within the resource, structural and volume envelopes.
label: Non-Causal

text: The interface plate should allow for additional capability of long duration stare/pointing.
label: Non-Causal

text: Quantities and locations will be defined in <TBD-L2-GW-065> for utilization planning and module procurement.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide a robotically compatible science airlock.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: To support science and utilization of robotic transfer of payloads and ORUs into/out of the Science Airlock by both internal and external robotics.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide redundant robotic translation paths and utilization access (single- fault tolerance).
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Ensures that any single LPGF failure cannot trap the arm or eliminate access for utilization and maintenance.
label: Non-Causal

text: Translation paths need to be designed according to manipulator reach and maintained to be free of obstructions.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall support external robotics performing end-over-end translation to perform its functions on all external surfaces of the Gateway where robotics activities are planned.
label: Non-Causal

text: The external robotic manipulators are expected to be dual-ended with walk- over capability, and a moving base analogous to ISS-MBS is not planned.
label: Non-Causal

text: In order to fulfill the operational need, it has to translate around the Gateway in order to execute its functions.
label: Causal

text: This includes reconfiguring the TTE network and the power distribution network.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Gateway needs to provide spaced out base points for External Robotic manipulators to access the areas where activities are planned to take place.
label: Causal

text: To do this, Gateway needs to attach grapple fixtures to structural hard points and route cabling to the connectors.
label: Causal

text: The coverage of Gateway will be assessed and analyzed to determine the location requirements.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall have an external robotic system capable of autonomous operations that implements the following functions on the exterior of Gateway: inspection, installation and removal of payloads, transfer of equipment through the science airlock, off-loading and re- loading of logistics vehicles, free-flying vehicle capture and release, lunar and planetary mission equipment transfer, lunar and planetary element assembly, berthing and unberthing of modules and vehicles, removal and replacement of ORUs, self-maintenance, and assistance to EVA.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: This provides the list of primary functions that EVR will furnish to Gateway, and which Gateway needs to support with the appropriate infrastructure.
label: Non-Causal

text: The functions are intended to be autonomous to eliminate dependence on crew presence, to reduce communication and control resource usage on the ground, to reduce operational lifecycle costs and to be a proving ground for path to Mars.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall limit disturbances to the vehicle and robotics, during sensitive External Robotic operations, to a level <TBD-L2-GW-014> that will not affect robot performance and safety, without the need for flight-specific analysis, including after a single failure.
label: Causal

text: Rationale: Based on ISS experience, attitude and orbit control systems need to have a passive mode to minimize disturbances during robotic ops.
label: Causal

text: On ISS this involved selection of a Torque Equilibrium Attitude (TEA) to maximize CMG control capacity, controlling exercise, not performing dockings or orbital maintenance, and inhibiting CMG desaturations when the robotic hardware was within 2 ft of structure.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall support a network with a TTE end-over-end translation of the external robotics.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Robotic end-to-end relocation will require a reconfiguration of TTE topology, as well as payload and ORU mate/demate operations.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall support self-deployment of the EVR Element upon initial delivery.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: When the logistics module arrives at Gateway, there will likely be no crew to assist, and EVA time is not meant to be expended on nominal operations even if they were there.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall comply with applicable requirements in DSG-SPEC-IVR-013, Gateway Program Subsystem Specification for Intravehicular Robotics.
label: Non-Causal

text: To promote the successful integration between the internal robotics and the Gateway modules and systems, a set of requirements that dictates interface, performance, and functions was developed.
label: Causal

text: Adherence to this subsystem specification will ensure that the internal robotics system can successfully achieve its tasks and goals while minimizing the overall impact to the Gateway.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide the ability to access and service designated internal payloads and logistics without the need for crew intervention.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: During uncrewed periods, payloads and logistics will be delivered to the Gateway and will need to be able to be extracted, moved, unpacked, installed, operated, maintained and serviced.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall have internal robotic assets capable of inspection.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Per requirement of dormancy / uncrewed periods of up to 3 years (HEOMD-01: DSG-R-5), multiple activities in Gateway may require mobile robots, or robots with dexterous manipulation capability, to perform detailed inspections.
label: Causal

text: IVR can be controlled either autonomously or with assistance from Earth-based mission control.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall support internal robotics access between modules.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: During uncrewed periods, internal robotics must be able to either pass through open hatches or pass objects through open hatches to successfully accomplish most tasks.
label: Causal

text: Based on vestibule length, this might include the need for IVR translation aids near the hatch or even in the vestibule.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide a method for determining and communicating internal location information that is common to internal robotics and human operators (crew and ground).
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway needs to provide a similar approach and a common language for discussing location that satisfies both robotic and human needs.
label: Non-Causal

text: Complexity of a robotic system is greatly reduced if an appropriate markings system is used to simplify identification and localization.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall ensure that payloads, equipment, and tools used by internal robotics have interfaces for both humans and robots.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: This will ensure all locations accessible by internal robotics is also accessible to crew.
label: Causal

text: Complexity of a robotic system is greatly reduced if design of human interfaces also considers robotic manipulation.
label: Causal

text: Equipment includes systems that are maintainable and repairable.
label: Non-Causal

text: These interfaces and any possible adapters will be covered in the IVR ICD.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide stowage and charging interfaces to support internal robotics operations.
label: Causal

text: Rationale: Gateway needs to distribute resources required to support internal robotics operations to the modules where internal robotics operations are performed.
label: Causal

text: In particular, certain modules will need to serve as "home base" for IVR system components.
label: Non-Causal

text: These docking stations will include room for IVR stowage as well as charging and network interfaces.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide a reconfigurable mobile video camera system for inspection and internal robotic operations support.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Robotic tasks can be aided by a free flying camera providing a "bird's eye view", however, this view can be moved/vary between and during tasks.
label: Causal

text: This will be compatible with internal wireless communications.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall use robotically compatible interfaces to allow the IVR system to access/retrieve/install internal logistics cargo.
label: Causal

text: Rationale: To help reduce crew time required for logistics management during the 30 day mission, the modules should use robotically compatible interfaces to allow the IVR system to access/retrieve/install logistics cargo.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide resources and interfaces for Utilization payloads and payload accommodations as defined in the Gateway Utilization Payload Interface Requirement Document <TBD-L2-GW-062>.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Gateway is intended to support diverse science, (along with associated exploration), activities and close Strategic Knowledge Gaps.
label: Non-Causal

text: Gateway will accommodate crewed and uncrewed placement and operation of science assets e.g. internal investigations, external packages, In Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) operations, transfer of surface samples, sample return to Earth, and science data collection/transfer.
label: Non-Causal

text: Operations of the Gateway will also include a robotic arm for installing experiments, a science airlock, and the ability to conduct operations on each element.
label: Non-Causal

text: Internal and external payloads will be operated during crewed and uncrewed periods.
label: Causal

text: Payloads will need the specified Gateway resources available during operations.
label: Causal

text: Most payloads would not require crew interaction (likely apart from instrument installation and setup) and would continue to operate during uncrewed periods.
label: Causal

text: Resource interfaces between Gateway modules and the internal research accommodations (facilities) and between the accommodations and the payloads need to be standardized throughout Gateway.
label: Causal

text: Maximizes placement flexibility for internal payload facilities and payloads.
label: Causal

text: Minimizes flight hardware development to support payloads.
label: Causal

text: Minimizes ground support equipment for hardware test.
label: Causal

text: The Gateway shall allocate a minimum of 5.15 Tbits/day (644 GB/day) for utilization use.
label: Non-Causal

text: Rationale: Out of the total 7.49Tbits per day data downlink capacity, 5.15 T/Bits per day is allocated for utilization (science & technology demonstrations) use.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Gateway shall provide a minimum of three (3) cubic meters (m3) of internal volume for powered payload locations.
label: Causal

text: Gateway will accommodate crewed and uncrewed placement and operation of science assets e.g. internal investigations, external packages, ISRU operations, transfer of surface samples, sample return to Earth, and science data collection/transfer.

text: KSC-DE-512-SM establishes requirements and guidance for design and fabrication of ground systems (GS) that includes: ground support equipment (GSE), ground support systems (GSS), and facility ground support systems (F-GSS) to provide uniform methods and processes for design and development of robust, safe, reliable, maintainable, supportable, and cost-effective GS in support of space flight and institutional programs and projects.
label: Non-Causal

text: This standard is intended to supplement the minimum requirements of NASA-STD-5005 by applying more stringent, restrictive, or demanding requirements applicable to the specific KSC environment.
label: Non-Causal

text: This standard also provides requirements for GSS and F-GSS because these systems are not covered in NASA-STD-5005.

text: The criticality of a system failure mode will be assigned on the basis of worst-case credible failure effect, assuming the loss of all redundancy (where applicable).

text: The analysis of the TSRV FCS was carried out using a Boeing-developed Object Oriented Analysis (OOA) methodology.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Boeing OOA method unifies traditional systems analysis methods of information modeling, process modeling (e.g., Yourdon-DeMarco Structured Analysis), and behavior modeling (e.g., Ward-Mellor Real-Time Extensions) into a single mure powerful method which synergistically combines the strengths of all three methods.
label: Non-Causal

text: See References [8], [lo], [ll], and [12] for background information.
label: Non-Causal

text: OOA is an alternative to “structured analysis” as a requirements specification language.
label: Non-Causal

text: It unifies elements of information, behavior, and processing on an atomic level (object level), whereas structured analysis provides three hierarchical system level views which are not necessarily consistent and require parallel maintenance.
label: Causal

text: OOA provides a method to rigorously define the requirements of any complex system in such a way that the analyst can readily identify any missing or contradictory requirements.
label: Non-Causal

text: The result is a complete, consistent, and simplified description of a system’s essential requirements.
label: Causal

text: Furthermore, OOA provides a solid foundation for partitioning systems into “objects” and results in a system definition which allows a smooth transition into design.
label: Causal

text: Object oriented specifications map very easily into object-oriented design and object-oriented programming (using languages such as Ada, Objective Cy and Smalltalk), but also may be readily translated into other design schemes such as a standard hierarchical structured design.
label: Non-Causal

text: OOA’s partitioning methodology and design flexibility are a few of the features which make it particularly suited to the goal of defining alternate architectures for an existing complex system.
label: Non-Causal

text: OOA partitions a system into objects, or object classes.
label: Non-Causal

text: The goals of OOA are to assist in the “discovery” of the object classes in a system and the relationships between those object classes; and 2) to provide a mechanism to document those object classes so that they can be verified and later communicated to designers and programmers.

text: The “products” of OOA and the relationships between them are depicted in Figure 5.2.

text: The products are the deliverable results of applying OOA to a specific system.
label: Causal

text: In other words, they are the graphic and textual models that are produced by the process of analysis.
label: Non-Causal

text: The products of OOA describe the system at two conceptual levels of detail: clars level models and system level models.
label: Non-Causal

text: Class level models provide the detailed internal views of single object classes.
label: Non-Causal

text: System level models, on the other hand, describe the way object classes fit together to make the system as a whole.
label: Non-Causal

text: The system level models are not concerned with the internal details of the object classes.
label: Non-Causal

text: Likewise, the internal “schematic” of each object class must not concern itself with any other object class directly (i.e., knowledge of the internal workings of another object class is not allowed).
label: Non-Causal

text: These rules support the principle of information hiding.
label: Non-Causal

text: An object class can be thought of as a template that represents the generic form of all objects which belong to that class.
label: Non-Causal

text: Object classes can be described by the data they carry, the processes they perform, and the behavior they exhibit.
label: Non-Causal

text: Therefore, each object class template is comprised of three class level models: a Data Model; 2) a Process Model; and 3) a Behavior Model.
label: Causal

text: In order for an object to be a member of a given class, it must conform to the class’ template: that is, it must be &scribed by the prescribed data, it must do the prescribed work (processing), and it must exhibit the prescribed behavior.
label: Causal

text: The data aspect of an object class is described textually by a set of Attributes.
label: Non-Causal

text: Each attribute represents a single meaningful fact that is pertinent to, and necessary for, all instances of that class.
label: Non-Causal

text: The set of attributes for an object class defines the information that is relevant for that class.
label: Non-Causal

text: The Process Model captures the functionality of an object class,.
label: Non-Causal

text: The model defines the set of P rocesses that operate upon or manipulate objects within that class.

label: Non-Causal

text: The Structured Analysis “minispec” is a convenient mechanism for describing the details of a process.

text: The behavior aspect of an object class is described by a finite state automaton.

text: A strategy serves the purpose of guiding the analyst toward the goal of completing the analysis, and different strategies may be appropriate in different situations.
label: Non-Causal

text: The analysis strategy used here was necessarily oriented toward the OOA methodology.
label: Non-Causal

text: The strategy was to develop the OOA models (see 5.3) of the system requirements using an information centered approach.
label: Non-Causal

text: With this strategy, the analyst focuses frrst on the information aspect of a system in order to discover as many of the object classes as possible.
label: Causal

text: The result of this activity is a fmt approximation of the OCRM along with Data Models for each of the object classes found so far.
label: Causal

text: Note that at this stage, those objects with little or no data (i.e., those which are more process and/or behavior intensive) have not necessariiy been discovered: the list and definitions of the object classes are likely to be incomplete at this juncture.

text: As subsequent phases of analysis (e.g., behavior and process modeling) are pedomed, new object classes may be discovered, or a few existing ones may be combined or split up.

text: The next step involves modeling the processing aspect of the system by developing a Process Model for each object class.

text: A variety of definitions exists for terms associated with the retrieval, validation and exploitation of land, lake and ice surface temperatures.
